pool.text: General William Larimer and Captain Jonathan Cox placed cottonwood logs to stake a claim.
The Denver City, Kansas Territory, post office opened for local residents.
Six chiefs of the Southern Cheyenne and four of the Arapaho signed a treaty.
Denver City shortened its name to Denver with its newfound importance.
Citizens cheered as the Denver Pacific completed the link to the transcontinental railroad.
The precursor to the international charity United Way was formed in Denver.
Continental Airlines moved its headquarters to Stapleton Airport in Denver.
Denver established its relationship with Brest, France, creating the second-oldest sister city.
The original Frontier Airlines began operations at Denver's old Stapleton International Airport.
Scott's Liquid Gold, Inc. has been making furniture polish in Denver.
Village Inn restaurants began as a single pancake house in Denver.
Big O Tires of Centennial opened its first franchise in Denver.
Lowry Air Force Base ceased its flight operations before eventually closing down.
Rodolfo Corky Gonzales hosted the First National Chicano Youth Liberation Conference in March.
The Shane Company sold its first diamond jewelry in Denver.
Johns Manville Corp. relocated its headquarters to Denver from New York.
Re/Max made Denver its headquarters.
CH2M Hill relocated from Oregon to the Denver Technological Center.
Denver hosted the World Theatre Festival at the Denver Center for Performing Arts.
Voters approved FasTracks, a massive commuter rail, light rail, and bus expansion project.
